videos.script: Four numbers, four, nine, ten and thirteen. Combine them with plus, minus, times and divide, and make twenty-four. {{puzzle}} A chain of thought tries one first step and follows it to the end. If the first step was a dead end, the whole chain is wasted. {{chain}} A tree of thoughts proposes several first steps instead. It judges each one: can twenty-four still be reached from here? It keeps the promising ones and drops the rest. {{judge}} Then it does the same again from every step it kept. {{level}} In this lesson you watch that search run, level by level, on a real program. You change how many branches it keeps, and give it four numbers that have no answer at all. {{run}} Then you see what it costs when a model does the proposing and the judging. Many calls for one answer, which only pays on the right kind of problem. {{cost}}
